'''Kathleen J. Green''' is a [[cell biologist]] whose research focuses on how cell-cell communication drives tissue form and function.<ref name="Lab">{{cite web |title=Kathleen Green Lab |url=https://labs.feinberg.northwestern.edu/green/ |website=[[Feinberg School of Medicine]] |publisher=[[Northwestern University]] |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref> She is the Joseph L. Mayberry Professor of Pathology and Toxicology and Professor of [[Dermatology]] at [[Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine]] in Chicago.<ref name="Lab"/> She also serves as Associate Director of Basic Sciences at the Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center of Northwestern University.<ref>{{cite web |title=Green Appointed Associate Director for Basic Sciences Research |url=https://www.cancer.northwestern.edu/news/2014/Green-Basic-Sciences.html |website=Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center of Northwestern University |access-date=23 April 2021 |archive-date=8 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210708204656/https://www.cancer.northwestern.edu/news/2014/Green-Basic-Sciences.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Green received her B.A. in Biology from [[Pomona College]] in Claremont, California. She went on to study with David L. Kirk at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] where she studied development in the model organism [[Volvox carteri]]. She obtained her PhD in [[Cell and Developmental Biology]] in 1982. After obtaining her PhD Green moved to Chicago where she carried out postdoctoral training at [[Northwestern University Medical School]] in the laboratory of [[Robert D. Goldman]], whose work included the identification and characterization of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton.  Toward the end of this time period, Dr. Green set out to clone, sequence and characterize desmoplakin, an essential molecule that links the intermediate filament cytoskeleton to intercellular junctions known as desmosomes. Her work on desmoplakin laid the foundation for an independent career beginning in 1987 as a faculty member in the Department of [[Pathology]] at Northwestern.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fleischman |first1=John |title=ASCB Profile: Kathy Green |url=https://www.ascb.org/files/0711profile.pdf |website=www.ascb.org |publisher=American Society for Cell Biology |access-date=27 April 2021}}</ref> 

==Leadership and service==
Green is the Deputy Editor-in Chief of the [[Journal of Cell Science]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Editor biographies |url=https://journals.biologists.com/jcs/pages/editor-bios |website=Journal of Cell Science |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref>
